time.description:
Time is when the request was made. A tool that has no clock keeps the
order and leaves it unset.

from.description:
From and To are the capturing tool's labels for the sender and the
receiver, kept as written. A binding maps them to participants.

requestId.description:
RequestID is the value of a request ID header, when the capture has
one. It joins client events and other sources to the exchange.

bodyTruncated.description: BodyTruncated reports that a body was cut at the size limit.

label.description:
Label is a name a tool gave the exchange, such as a Newman request's
name. It never changes a match.

annotations.description:
Annotations are evidence a tool produced about the exchange, such as
assertions or a client's own events. They never change a match.

Exchange.description: Exchange is one HTTP request and its response.

kind.description: Kind classifies the annotation, such as "assertion" or "client-event".

text.description: Text is the annotation as a person reads it.

ok.description: OK is the result of an assertion; unset for other kinds.

time.description:
Time is when the annotated event happened, when it differs from the
exchange's time.

ExchangeAnnotation.description: ExchangeAnnotation is a piece of evidence about an exchange.

format.description: Format names the format and its major version: pidl-observation/v1.

source.description: Source says which tool produced the observation and what it covers.

exchanges.description: Exchanges are the requests and responses, in the order they happened.

Observation.description: Observation is a captured run of a real system: the HTTP exchanges it made, in order, whatever tool captured them.

tool.description:
Tool names the tool that captured the exchanges, such as
"aauth-sandbox", "har" or "newman".

requestFidelity.description: RequestFidelity is wire or client; empty when unknown.

from.description: From and To bound the time the observation covers.

ObservationSource.description: ObservationSource describes where an observation came from.

ObservedHeaders.description: ObservedHeaders are header fields as name and value pairs, in their original order and case.

body.description:
Body is a JSON value for a JSON body, a JSON string for other text,
or {"base64": "…", "mediaType": "…"} for binary content.

ObservedRequest.description: ObservedRequest is a captured HTTP request.

body.description: Body is encoded as ObservedRequest.Body is.

ObservedResponse.description: ObservedResponse is a captured HTTP response.

title: PIDL Observation
description: A captured run of a real system: its HTTP exchanges in order, whatever tool captured them, matched to a document's steps by `pidl generate --observation`.
